summary: The paper presents a reusable design for data distributions built from domains, index sets, data collections and extensible distribution classes that map each index to a unit of locality and a local layout. It outlines how the Chapel language realizes this design, but it reports no empirical evaluation.
why_read: It gives a newcomer a compact, language-independent vocabulary for user-defined data distributions and shows how one language expresses them.
main_contribution: A reusable, extensible design pattern for data distributions, with an outline of its realization in Chapel.
main_limitation: The paper states that full user freedom in specifying distributions raises the burden of ensuring good run-time performance, and that efficiency evaluation is still in progress.
notes: Title, first author (Roxana E. Diaconescu) and author list match the title page. Not confirmed from the PDF text layer: the venue (Workshop on Patterns in High Performance Computing) and the year 2005. The PDF creation date is 2005-05-12 and the reference list ends at 2004.
